findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: The purpose of `birthday` and `phone` is the greeting, and the opt-in is their only reason to exist. Define what opting out does: when a member turns greetings off, clear both columns on `profiles` (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 7(3) withdrawal of consent). Add a requirement and a scenario ("WHEN a member opts out THEN their birthday and phone are erased") to the spec, and a task to implement and test it. Today a member who opts out keeps their birth date and phone number in `profiles` until the whole profile is deleted.
findings.title: Birthday and phone kept after the member opts out

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: The design copies `birthday` and `phone` into the nightly backups but states no expiry for those copies, so a member's birth date and phone number erased from `profiles` (opt-out or account deletion) survive in every backup indefinitely. State the backup retention period that bounds how long erased data lingers, and how an erasure is honoured after a restore (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17).
findings.title: No retention period for the copies in the nightly backups

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: The spec only requires that "the service SHALL send them a text message"; nothing needs the member's name. Each day the job hands Textly, a US processor, the display name together with the phone number, beyond what the purpose needs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation). Send only the phone number and a message body that does not carry the name, or state in the spec why the name is needed in the message.
findings.title: Display name sent to Textly when the greeting only needs the phone

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: Textly is identified as a new processor receiving phone numbers outside the EEA. Which transfer mechanism covers it (EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification or standard contractual clauses, GDPR Chapter V), and is a processor agreement in place (Art. 28)? Record the answer in the design; only the controller can confirm it.
findings.title: Transfer to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard or processor agreement

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the purpose is stated (birthday messages wanted by marketing) but not the lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6). The opt-in suggests consent; if so, say so in the proposal, and make sure the opt-in wording states the purpose and that it can be withdrawn.
findings.title: Lawful basis for the birthday data is not stated
